patch_resolves_note: The frozen required root assertion verifies differentially: vulnerable mrb_funcall_with_block leaves argv != mrb->c->stbase + voff after stack growth, while the patched fixed source repairs argv before the later stack_copy(). However, the patched fixed execution in this staged non-ARVO environment still exited with rc=134, so overall crash disappearance was not established here even though the selected source-level obligation was satisfied at the protected event.

root_cause_criterion.criterion: When argv aliases the current VM stack, stack growth must refresh argv so argv == mrb->c->stbase + voff before any later direct stack_copy() of those arguments.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable path records the stack offset but leaves the local argv alias stale across mrb_stack_extend(); the fixed path satisfies the missing refresh before the protected stack_copy() executes.

nodes.state: At the stack-resident argv check, the recorded offset voff names the current stack-backed argv location, so argv == mrb->c->stbase + voff.
The vulnerable witness takes a stack-growth path where mrb_stack_extend() moves the VM stack base, freeing the old stack storage that argv still points into unless it is repaired.
The stack_copy() sink receives the same local argv-derived pointer as its src operand, so the stale alias is the value dereferenced by memcpy().

edges.relation: The same stack-backed argv pointer survives across the stack-growth operation until the post-extend use site.
The unrepaired post-extend argv pointer is passed directly as the stack_copy() source.
